name: development
description: General development workflow skills for committing, branch naming, and other git operations, plus the shared telemetry/v1 emit + validate contract, its stream-generic rollup, and a committed Grafana reference dashboard for the cross-repo hand-off; ships a PreToolUse(Agent) hook, inert unless switch_fable_to_opus is truthy, that then redirects dispatches whose effective model is fable to opus; bootstrap also ships the blessed Spring, non-Spring-Java, Python and Go resilience + dependency-health payloads (resilience4j for the JVM, circuitbreaker+tenacity for Python, sony/gobreaker for Go, wired to the ops-api /health surface — versioned v1/v2, where v2 serves RFC 9457 problem+json on the two probe 503s while v1 stays frozen, #1330). Gathers kubernetes/IaC findings (Helm/Kustomize/Argo CD manifest presence, Kyverno policy + policy-test detection) for the development-kubernetes topic dispatcher, and OpenTofu/Terraform findings (tofu fmt/validate/tflint/trivy presence detection, plus evaluated state-encryption and pinned-Conftest policy + policy-test checks over *.tf) for the development-opentofu topic dispatcher. Bootstrap also ships the no-cluster-deploy required status check, which fails an application repo whose workflows deploy straight to a cluster (the app-repo half of the image-promotion contract). NOTE for existing repos: a re-run of bootstrap now installs ops-api v2 payloads, whose two probe 503s return RFC 9457 problem+json instead of the v1 {"status":"down"} envelope — see the ops-surface how-to before re-running. ALSO for existing repos: bootstrap's .spectral.yaml is now a thin shim extending one EXACT pinned org styleguide ruleset over jsDelivr (#689) instead of the #692 starter, so a re-run replaces a local ruleset with a remote pin and enforces fifteen org rules at error (four of them a warn->error promotion relative to the #692 starter, nine newly minted) — review the api-styleguide how-to before re-running, and note contracts-lint now needs network access to jsDelivr on every run (no offline fallback, by design), so restricted CI egress or a CDN outage fails the lint until it recovers. resolve-issue detects the repo type at §1b (review-dispatch.zsh detect) and loads the matching development-<repo_type>:resolve-profile when one exists, continuing with its generic rules when none does (#1504). A human's interactive round grant is now persisted mechanically rather than remembered: record-grant.zsh writes the granted ceiling to <work-dir>/.max-rounds and resolve-story-loop.zsh --resume adopts it, reporting the ceiling in force as the new always-present effective_max_rounds / max_rounds_source status keys while max_rounds keeps reporting the value the caller passed (#1576). Residue condition 2 is removed (#1571): the review loop's CONVERGED_WITH_RESIDUE terminal no longer requires every remaining blocker to sit in the previous round's fix-touched set, because scope-findings already confines each round's findings to the story diff — which made the terminal unreachable from the very closing sweep it was built for, since a promoting round runs no fix pass and its set is empty by design. The terminal is correspondingly BROADER: residue now holds on almost any zero-CRITICAL non-convergence, so runs that previously ended in a human escalation may instead open a PR and file the remainder as follow-up issues - and the #1498 possible-false-trip auto-continue is now tried BEFORE residue at that rung, so the loop still spends its free round rather than shipping. resolve-issue's review loop now hands each reviewer a scope block carrying both the repo-relative and absolute spelling of every file plus a verbatim opener naming the worktree to read, and review-dispatch.zsh plan emits worktree_root/original_root/scope_abs — a repo-root file read from the original checkout produced a CRITICAL false positive (#1582). review-dispatch.zsh now applies ONE anchoring rule for --repo: it names the REPOSITORY and every subcommand resolves it to the git toplevel before anything derived is read, so detection, the .maintenance.yml primary and the default findings_path (now absolute, <worktree_root>/.review/findings-round-<N>.json) all describe the same tree, and a subdirectory --repo is a spelling of its repository rather than a scope filter (#1587). bootstrap's IaC path gains the gate MECHANISM (#1603, epic #1602): templates/iac/scripts/k8s-gate.zsh.tmpl, one locally runnable script running render (helm template + kustomize build --enable-helm, so helmCharts: overlays inflate) → schema → lint → policy → config-scan (the pinned trivy binary, embedded checks) → argocd against the rendered tree, one `gate: <stage> ok|skipped — <reason>|FAILED` verdict line per stage, stopping at the first red, every skip reported (an empty repository is green), a missing tool refused before any stage with its brew line, and a developer's working tree left untouched (a symlink-shared policy set is evaluated through a same-depth sibling mirror, never swapped in place). #1604 wires it: kubernetes-ci.yml.tmpl is now ONE job, `gate`, that installs zsh and all seven gate tools at step-level pins (the pins tests/iac-tools.zsh reads for the fixture harness) and runs the repo's gate command, {{GATE_COMMAND}} (render.zsh --gate-command, default make lint, an empty value refused); Makefile.tmpl (lint runs the gate script, hooks sets core.hooksPath) and a two-line hooks/pre-push.tmpl run the same command locally, .maintenance.yml records it as gate: on the kubernetes primary (a KUBERNETES render block), render.zsh carries a template's executable bit to its output, and the gate script and hook are stamped and drift-tracked. #1606 moves IaC-mode branch protection onto it too: branch-protection.sh's IaC mode now requires the single `gate` context instead of the six retired per-stage contexts, and refuses (exit 1, before writing any rule) when .github/workflows/kubernetes-ci.yml cannot report `gate`: it is absent, has no `gate` job, or its `gate` job carries `name:`, a `strategy:` block or a reusable-workflow `uses:` (GitHub would then report the check under another name) - so on an existing IaC repo re-render kubernetes-ci.yml with bootstrap first (that refresh applies to a plugin-rendered file; a hand-written one needs a `gate` job added by hand), then re-run branch protection to drop the six from its rule. #1605 moves bootstrap's §3l flow onto the gate: it emits kubernetes-ci.yml, scripts/k8s-gate.zsh, hooks/pre-push and the Makefile, names the single `gate` context, wires the hook with the new install-iac-hooks.zsh instead of pre-commit (a wiring failure is reported and bootstrap continues), lets a repo with no kubernetes marker bootstrap onto the IaC path on an explicit empty-GitOps-repo confirmation at Q4, and gives preflight.sh an IaC mode that requires gh, jq, git and the gate's seven tools instead of the pre-commit and scanner set. #1583 gives the review loop a carry accounting: reviewers report each carried blocker as confirmed, re-raised (with evidence in the findings file) or unconfirmed, the conductor passes the per-identity records as --carry-accounting (hook mode: the panel's <findings-path>.carry.json sidecar), and the loop refuses a round (CARRY-UNACCOUNTED, exit 2, before verify-<R+1>.json is written) in which a carried blocker was neither confirmed nor re-raised, listing it in the status JSON's always-present carry_unconfirmed and stamping carry_accounting into every accepted round's changelist. #1584 makes a read-only reviewer's tool-verdict claim a SUGGESTION until the conductor runs the tool: resolve-issue §3.5's round protocol gains a *decided pass* that, after the gate has been observed green — or, on a round the boundary runs with no gate, after the panel — and before consolidation, runs every read-only `decides:` command a finding names — as written, never substituted — against the round's minted tree in the worktree root, records exit + first output lines to `<work-dir>/decided-<R>.log`, and rewrites the severity to the reviewer's `proposed-severity` only on a real red (a green and a command that could not run each leave it a logged SUGGESTION; a malformed finding is recorded and promotes nothing, its severity changed in neither direction). The pass settles a finding on the round that RAISES it; re-deciding a promotion the loop then carries is a stated KNOWN LIMITATION filed as #1647, and the reviewer half ships with every panel's read-only reviewers, repo-wide (#1644). consolidate-findings.zsh accepts an optional per-finding `decided` ("red"|"green") and carries it onto every changelist item, blocking and suggestions alike, as a visible RECORD — never a mechanism, so it sets no severity, priority or blocking; on dedup only group members sharing the representative title contribute (an empty title is not a match key), a red anywhere in the group additionally exempts the item from the `--adjudicated` drop, and a finding without the field is byte-identical to before. Since #1485 resolve-story-loop.zsh refuses a FULL round whose scope is empty — no story diff, or only loop-owned files changed — as STALE_FINDINGS (the EMPTY-STORY-DIFF arm), whether its panel wrote no findings file or an actual [], instead of converging on a review that saw nothing. register-claude-apps.zsh keeps ONE registry entry PER OWNER (#1682): --org <slug> registers an organisation's App pair beside the personal one (organisation-owner rights checked before the browser opens), --apps <list> registers a subset (--apps claude-maintenance is writer-only), apps.json becomes schema 2 keyed by owner with Keychain services claude-plugins.<owner>.<app>, and a schema-1 apps.json is migrated in place on first use (backup at apps.json.v1.bak); owner keys are lower-cased. Every consumer now picks the App pair by the OWNER OF THE CURRENT REPOSITORY (#1683): the mint scripts, install-claude-apps.zsh (including --writer-only), bootstrap's --claude-approver auto-detection and its Step 4.5 preflight share one helper, claude-apps-owner.zsh (status reports each App as registered, not registered or key missing for that owner), so an organisation repo mints the organisation's App and a personal repo the personal one with no flag; a missing owner or App fails with the exact register-claude-apps.zsh [--org <slug>] --apps <app> command and never falls through to another owner, and a schema-1 apps.json is refused naming register-claude-apps.zsh --list. The #1682 compatibility aliases are gone: the next register-claude-apps.zsh run deletes the legacy Keychain items first and only then drops the top-level keys and alias_owner from apps.json, retrying on the next run when a delete fails. /development:resolve-issue now emits its own telemetry/v1 record (#1226): a single-issue run that reaches the dependency precheck appends exactly one pipeline:"resolve-issue" record at whichever ending it reaches (success on a PR, parked at the readiness gate or the precheck, escalated, failed; a Step 0 stop appends none), through story-telemetry.zsh and the pure payload builder build-story-telemetry-record.zsh, and it is never fatal. The skill takes --telemetry-file PATH / --telemetry-dir DIR in any position and forwards them, with a pre-minted --parent-run-id, to every resolve-story-loop.zsh invocation, which gains both flags, a <work-dir>/.telemetry-run-ids ledger and an in-repo --telemetry-dir loop-internal exclusion; ARCHITECTURE.md records the per-pipeline instrumentation conventions every later pipeline follows. Bootstrap now composes its quality workflows, setup guide and pre-commit config per resolved tool instead of from two whole visibility trees (#1670): toolchain-templates.zsh selects the tool-scoped templates and render.zsh's per-tool block tags compose the jobs, so every toolchain resolve-tools.zsh accepts is composed; resolve-tools.zsh now also rejects CodeQL on a private repository (it needs GitHub Advanced Security). Branch protection, the setup preflight and State D's gap-fill now take that resolved toolchain instead of visibility (#1671): branch-protection.sh and preflight.sh take --static-analysis / --vulnerabilities and no longer accept a visibility flag, the required contexts follow the #1670 D1 rule (analyze (<lang>) only when codeql.yml is on disk), preflight checks each resolved tool's prerequisites, Step 4.5's setup automation runs one script per tool under that tool's own trigger (setup-sonarcloud.sh, setup-sonarqube.sh, register-runner.sh, setup-snyk.sh, enable-github-security.sh) and never re-applies branch protection, which Step 4b applies once (#1769), and bootstrap no longer stops at its plan for a non-default toolchain. resolve-issue runs a story size pre-flight before its first edit (#1437): the session declares the files it intends to touch, size-preflight.zsh stops a plan over its file-count threshold, one that straddles plugins or one that edits bootstrap templates together with any other owned file outside the bootstrap skill, and a stop is overridden by the human or parked with the needs-split label; every verdict is a story-preflight telemetry record. resolve-issue now applies a loaded resolve-profile's Fix-pass rules heading at every §3.5 fix pass and its Documentation expectations heading at §2's same-PR user-docs step, skipping a heading whose body begins with none; Residue joins Panel as a record no step dereferences, and the #1506 deferral is retired (#1805).
